synthesis: Scout drivers authenticate via email+password (ClarityScoutAuthController, Sanctum bearer token). Initial onboarding uses a 7-day signed URL → set-password flow (ScoutSetPasswordController) that becomes one-shot once `email_verified_at` is set (line 71-73 guard). If a user forgets their email OR password post-onboarding, they have ZERO recovery path—neither self-serve nor admin-assisted. The admin 'resend onboarding' action (ScoutUsersResource:356-412) is explicitly hidden once `email_verified_at` exists (line 368-369), and no password-reset mechanism exists. Clarity's admin/client panels use a fully-built passwordless OTP system (CustomLoginPage + OneTimePassword class, 6-digit cache-backed code with password_timeout TTL). The ticket requests adding Scout account recovery, preferring OTP/magic-link (Clarity-consistent) with an admin backstop so users are never permanently locked out. Critical architectural gap: Clarity's OTP returns a JWT token (OneTimePassword::attempt line 70), but Scout needs Sanctum bearer tokens; the OTP flow would need adaptation. prior onboarding signed-URL work precedent shows Scout's signed-URL infrastructure is robust (absolute+relative validation, friendly error pages), making a signed reset-link approach viable.

in_scope: Add OTP-based passwordless login to Scout PWA (parallel to existing email+password, not replacing it unless Q2 = replace)
Modify ClarityScoutAuthController to accept OTP verification as an alternative authentication path
Add Scout-specific OTP send/verify API endpoints under /api/scout/auth/* (throttled: send-otp, verify-otp)
Extend Clarity's OneTimePassword class or create ScoutOneTimePassword to return Sanctum token instead of JWT
Add 'Forgot Password?' link to Scout Login.vue → OTP send flow
Add admin password-reset action to ScoutUsersResource, visible for verified users, sends signed URL or triggers OTP
Optionally extend ScoutSetPasswordController to handle both onboarding (email_verified_at IS NULL) and password-reset (email_verified_at NOT NULL) via a 'mode' parameter
Add ScoutPasswordResetNotification (or reuse ScoutOnboardingNotification with different copy)
Update Scout Login.vue to support OTP entry UI (similar to Clarity CustomLoginPage two-step flow)
Add tests for OTP send/verify, admin reset action, signed URL reset flow, org-scoping
out_of_scope: Replacing password-based login entirely (ticket says PREFERRED not REQUIRED; Q2 unresolved)
Migrating existing Scout users to OTP-only (breaking change, not requested)
Adding OTP to Clarity admin/client (they already have it)
Changing Clarity's OTP TTL or JWT behavior (don't touch CustomLoginPage/OneTimePassword if possible)
Rewiring Laravel's password_reset_tokens table (it exists but unused; don't couple to it unless adopting Laravel's ForgotPasswordController)
Admin bulk password reset (single-user admin action is enough per AC2)
Force-login as recovery mechanism (it's impersonation, not user-owned recovery; prior force-login org-scoping work scoping risk)

open_questions.question: AC1 says 'without remembering email' but OTP/magic-link both require an email to receive the code/link. Interpretation: user remembers email (self-serve OTP) OR contacts admin (admin-assisted reset via force-login or signed link) if email is forgotten?
open_questions.why: AC1 'self-serve without remembering email or password' is contradictory for email-based recovery. Need confirmation: is 'forgot email' an explicit requirement (needs phone number or username fallback) or is it acceptable to say 'user must remember email OR contact admin'?

open_questions.question: Should OTP be an alternative to password (keep both, user chooses at login) or a replacement (password field removed from login, onboarding still sets password for admin/Filament access)?
open_questions.why: Impacts scope: alternative = add OTP endpoints + UI toggle, replacement = remove password field from Scout login + migrate existing users. Ticket says 'PREFERRED' for magic-link but doesn't mandate removing password. Both Clarity panels use OTP-only, so consistency suggests replacement, but Scout users may already have passwords memorized.

open_questions.question: Admin password-reset action: (A) signed URL that bypasses the one-shot guard and allows re-setting password, or (B) admin directly updates user password + sends email with new temp password (insecure), or (C) admin triggers OTP send so user can login via OTP then change password in-app?
open_questions.why: Three viable approaches: (A) reuses ScoutSetPasswordController infra + signed URL pattern (prior onboarding signed-URL work precedent), needs mode param to bypass hasVerifiedEmail guard; (B) violates best practice (admin shouldn't know user passwords); (C) cleanest UX but requires in-app password change UI (not mentioned in ticket). Need product decision.

open_questions.question: What TTL for OTP codes? Clarity uses config('auth.password_timeout') (default 900s = 15min). Scout onboarding uses 7 days for signed URLs. Should Scout OTP match Clarity's 15min or use a different value?
open_questions.why: Consistency favors 15min (matches Clarity), but if Scout users are in vehicles/field they may have sporadic connectivity. Could use 15min for in-app OTP, 7-day for admin-triggered signed reset link.

open_questions.question: Should the admin password-reset action be visible only to InsightLPR staff (admin_impersonator) or to all org admins? prior force-login org-scoping work precedent shows org-scoping is critical for Scout admin actions.
open_questions.why: Org admins being able to reset their drivers' passwords is reasonable (they already have force-login access), but needs confirmation. Ensure org-scoping: admin can only reset users in their own org (unless admin_impersonator).

open_questions.question: Non-production OTP bypass: Clarity's CustomLoginPage bypasses OTP in non-production (line 73-83). Should Scout's OTP flow also bypass in non-prod, or always require OTP (more realistic testing)?
open_questions.why: Consistency suggests bypass in non-prod, but Scout already requires password in all envs (no bypass). If OTP replaces password, bypass would be useful for local dev.

acceptance_criteria.text: Scout users can recover access via self-serve flow without remembering email OR password (magic-link/OTP preferred)
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: If Q1 = 'email must be remembered', this AC becomes: user enters email → receives OTP → can login. If Q1 = 'email can be forgotten', needs fallback (phone, username, or admin assist). Ticket says 'without remembering email' but OTP/magic-link both require email to send code/link. Likely intent: user remembers email OR contacts admin.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Testable once Q1 resolved. If email is required, test: enter email → OTP sent → enter OTP → logged in. If email can be forgotten, test: contact admin → admin sends reset link → user clicks → logged in.

acceptance_criteria.text: Admins can assist locked-out Scout users from the admin panel (password reset or magic-link resend)
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: ScoutUsersResource needs a new admin action (like resend_onboarding but for verified users) that either (A) sends a signed reset-link, (B) triggers OTP send, or (C) directly updates password. Design choice needed (Q3).
acceptance_criteria.notes: Testable with feature test: admin clicks reset action → user receives email → user follows link/OTP → can login. Must verify org-scoping (prior force-login org-scoping work): admin can only reset users in their own org (unless admin_impersonator).

acceptance_criteria.text: Recovery flow is consistent with Clarity's authentication (OTP/passwordless preferred over password reset)
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: Clarity admin/client use passwordless OTP. Consistency suggests Scout should also use OTP. But Q2 unresolved: is password kept as alternative or removed entirely? If removed, Scout becomes OTP-only like Clarity.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Subjective 'consistent with Clarity' AC. Testable as: Scout OTP flow matches Clarity's CustomLoginPage flow (email → send OTP → enter OTP → login). Use OneTimePassword class or equivalent.

acceptance_criteria.text: No permanent account lockout without an admin recovery path
acceptance_criteria.interpretation: Currently, a verified Scout user who forgets password is PERMANENTLY locked out (no self-serve, no admin action visible post-verification). After this ticket, either (1) self-serve OTP recovery OR (2) admin reset action must exist.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Testable by verifying: user forgets password → can recover via OTP (self-serve) OR admin can send reset link (admin-assisted). No scenario should result in 'call InsightLPR support to manually update DB'.

questions.question: Q1: Does 'without remembering email' mean email is optional for recovery (requires phone/username fallback) or is 'user must remember email OR contact admin' acceptable?
Q2: Should OTP be an alternative to password (keep both) or a replacement (remove password from Scout login)?
Q3: Admin password-reset action: (A) signed URL + re-use set-password flow, (B) direct password update (insecure), or (C) trigger OTP send?
Q4: What TTL for OTP codes? 15min (Clarity standard) or custom for Scout?
Q5: Should admin password-reset action be visible to all org admins or only InsightLPR staff?
Q6: Should Scout OTP bypass in non-production like Clarity does?

blockers.resolution: Product decision required. Recommendation: keep password as alternative initially (lower risk, no migration), add OTP as parallel path. Scout Login.vue shows 'Email + Password' OR 'Email + Get OTP' toggle.

blockers.resolution: Product decision required. Recommendation: signed URL (reuses ScoutSetPasswordController + prior onboarding signed-URL work validation infra, matches onboarding UX). Add 'mode' param: onboarding vs reset.

blockers.description: Architectural mismatch: OneTimePassword::attempt returns JWT (Auth::refresh line 70), Scout needs Sanctum token
blockers.resolution: Create ScoutOneTimePassword wrapper or add optional 'sanctum' mode to OneTimePassword::attempt. Precedent: ClarityScoutAuthController already mints Sanctum tokens (line 66), ScoutSetPasswordController also mints (line 44). Pattern exists.

notes.current_scout_auth: Email+password via /api/scout/login (ClarityScoutAuthController:21-87). Returns Sanctum bearer token ('clarity-scout-token', line 66). Checks: user exists, password valid, hasPermissionTo('clarity-scout'), kit_id not null, CLARITY_SCOUT feature active. Login throttled 5 attempts/minute (routes/api.php:29-33).
notes.current_onboarding: Admin grants clarity-scout permission → ScoutUserProvisioner sends ScoutOnboardingNotification (7-day signed URL) → user visits /scout/set-password/{user} → ScoutSetPasswordController shows form (GET) → user submits password (POST) → password saved, email_verified_at set (line 39-41), Sanctum token minted (line 44), user auto-logged into PWA. Signed URL becomes one-shot: guardUser() rejects if email_verified_at NOT NULL (line 71-73, 'reason: used').
notes.resend_onboarding_action: ScoutUsersResource:356-412. Visible ONLY if user has clarity-scout permission AND email_verified_at IS NULL (line 368-369). Sends fresh ScoutOnboardingNotification. Once user verifies, action disappears—this is the gap DEV-2575 addresses.
notes.clarity_otp_reference: CustomLoginPage (app/Filament/Auth/CustomLoginPage.php): two-step flow (email → send OTP button → OTP input field → login). OneTimePassword class (app/Filament/Auth/OneTimePassword.php): generates 6-digit code, caches as otp_{email} with TTL = config('auth.password_timeout') (default 900s = 15min). Non-production bypass: CustomLoginPage:73-83 skips OTP, logs in directly. OneTimePassword::attempt (line 59-75) returns JWT via Auth::refresh (line 70)—Scout needs Sanctum token instead.
notes.scout_frontend_login: resources/js/clarity-scout/views/Login.vue: simple email+password form (line 23-58), NO 'Forgot Password?' link. auth.login() calls /api/scout/login (stores/auth.js:93-125). Adding OTP flow requires: (1) 'Send OTP' button, (2) OTP input field (hidden until sent), (3) two-step form submission (send → verify).
notes.signed_url_infrastructure: ValidateScoutSignedUrl middleware (app/Http/Middleware/ValidateScoutSignedUrl.php) accepts both absolute and relative signed URLs (line 22: hasValidSignature(absolute: true) || hasValidSignature(absolute: false)). Renders friendly error pages (auth.scout.invalid-link) on failure. ScoutOnboardingNotification generates relative signature (line 28-33, absolute: false) to avoid TLS-termination issues (prior onboarding signed-URL work). Reusing this for password reset is viable.
notes.org_scoping_requirement: prior force-login org-scoping work precedent: Scout admin actions must stay org-scoped. Any password-reset action must ensure: (1) admin can only reset users in admin's org (unless admin_impersonator session), (2) ScoutSetPasswordController's guardUser() already checks org_id + clarity-scout permission (line 76-82). If reusing set-password route, no regression. If adding new admin action, must call setPermissionsTeamId($user->org_id) before permission checks.
notes.password_reset_tokens_table: Exists (database/migrations/0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php line 1) but UNUSED. Laravel's ForgotPasswordController / ResetPasswordController are NOT wired. Don't rely on this table unless adopting Laravel's password-reset flow (out of scope per precedent—Clarity uses OTP, not password_reset_tokens).
notes.test_coverage: ScoutSetPasswordControllerTest (13 tests): signed URL validation (absolute, relative, expired, unsigned), guardUser rejection (no permission, no org_id, already verified line 221-251), password submit success. ClarityScoutAuthControllerTest (20+ tests): login success, invalid credentials, missing permission, missing kit, throttling, logout, /me. No OTP tests exist yet—new tests required for OTP send/verify, admin reset action.
notes.design_recommendation: Recommend PHASED approach: (1) Phase 1: Add OTP as ALTERNATIVE to password (not replacement). Scout Login.vue shows toggle: 'Login with Password' or 'Login with OTP'. ClarityScoutAuthController gains /api/scout/auth/send-otp (throttled 5/min) and /api/scout/auth/verify-otp endpoints. OneTimePassword class extended or wrapped to return Sanctum token. (2) Phase 2: Admin reset action in ScoutUsersResource, visible for verified users, sends signed URL to /scout/reset-password/{user} (reuses ScoutSetPasswordController with mode=reset to bypass hasVerifiedEmail guard). (3) Phase 3 (optional, if Q2 = replace): remove password field from Scout Login.vue, keep password in onboarding so users still have password for admin/Filament if needed.

tables_affected.notes: Password reset updates users.password + keeps users.email_verified_at. Scout is Pro-only explicit-grant feature (small user subset). OTP send queries users.email (O(1) lookup).
OTP verify mints new Sanctum token, deletes prior clarity-scout-token (same single-token behavior as password login, ClarityScoutAuthController:64-66).

data_impact.notes: Auth operations are O(1) per-user lookups/writes. No batch processing, no data iteration, no scheduled commands. OTP codes cached (cache driver, not DB). No ClickHouse involvement (users table is PostgreSQL platform schema).
